basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 17.' and it opens '(Vers. 17 et 18.) Et audivit Deus Liam, et concepit, et peperit Jacob filium quintum, et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 17 et 18.) Et audivit Deus Liam, et concepit, et peperit Jacob filium quintum, et dixit Lia: Dedit Deus mercedem meam mihi, quia dedi ancillam meam viro meo: et vocavit nomen ejus Issachar. Etymologiam hujus nominis Septuaginta Interpretes ediderunt, est merces. Non utique, ut plerique addito pronomine male legunt, aestimandum est ita scriptum esse, quod est merces, sed totum nomen interpretatur, est merces. Is quippe dicitur est, יש, et SACHAR (שכר), merces. Hoc autem ideo, quia mandragoris filii Ruben introitum, qui Racheli debebatur, ad se viri emerat. Sequitur:
